instructions: Lay the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a heavy pan to an even 1/2 inch thickness.
In a small bowl, mix 3/4 tsp of the salt, 1/2 tsp of the pepper, 1/2 tsp of the cumin and 1/2 tsp of the smoked paprika. Pat the chicken dry and rub the mix over both sides.

Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium until it shimmers. Lay the chicken in and press it down. Leave it for 5 to 7 minutes, until the underside is golden brown and lets go of the pan.

Flip the chicken and cook the other side for 5 to 7 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when there's no pink left. Move it to a cutting board to rest for 10 minutes.

Drain the corn and pat it dry. Add it to the same pan over medium high and leave it for about 2 minutes, until some kernels are browned. Stir it and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's spotted brown all over. Transfer it to a plate to cool.
Meanwhile, make the dressing. Zest the lime until you have 1/2 tsp, then squeeze it. That should be about 2 tbsp juice. Finely chop 1 tbsp of the cilantro.

Whisk the 1/2 cup sour cream, the lime juice and zest, the 4 tsp honey, the chopped cilantro, the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin, the remaining 1/4 tsp smoked paprika, the 1/4 tsp garlic powder, the 1/4 tsp chili powder, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper in a small bowl.

Rinse and drain the black beans. Slice the romaine hearts crosswise into 1/2 inch ribbons. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice a quarter of the red onion. Slice the avocado. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
Slice the chicken against the grain into thin strips.

Toss the romaine with 1/4 cup of the dressing in a large bowl and divide it among 4 plates. Top them with the beans, corn, tomatoes, onion, avocado and chicken. Sprinkle 1/2 cup of the Monterey Jack over the four plates. Crush 1 cup of the tortilla chips over the top and scatter on the chopped cilantro.
Serve with the rest of the dressing on the side.
method_notes: All three put seasoned, pan cooked chicken breast over chopped romaine with corn, beans, cherry tomatoes, red onion, avocado, cheese and something crunchy, with a creamy lime dressing. Jessica Gavin (the lead) pounds the breasts thin and pan sears them with salt and pepper, uses a sour cream dressing with lime, honey and cumin, and adds pinto beans, zucchini and pepitas; The Anthony Kitchen and Whitney Bond use black beans and a spice rub on the chicken, which this version takes, and Whitney Bond adds crushed tortilla chips. The lead's dressing has minced jalapeño; it's left out here to keep it mild. No version had 20 ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no southwest chicken salad, so the top rated version read leads.
